clue.text: A duke, European or Chinese?

parts.note: taken as written
Sino- is the combining form meaning Chinese, as in Sino-Japanese

explanation.surface: A question about whether some duke comes from Europe or from China.
explanation.walkthrough: Duke Orsino rules Illyria in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night, so 'A duke, European' is the definition, leaving 'or Chinese' as plain wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Orsino is the Illyrian duke in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night, a European nobleman by name and setting.

clue.text: Poor boy regularly said to be upper-class?

indicators.note: a posh English speaker drops the T and says the word for frequently like 'orfen', so this signals how it sounds in such a mouth

parts.note: something done regularly is done often

explanation.surface: A poor lad who keeps being described as a toff, ironically.
explanation.walkthrough: The upper-class English pronunciation 'orfen' for the word meaning regularly is the joke; 'Poor boy' is the definition in the Dickensian sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A child without parents, like Oliver Twist, is the archetypal pitiable poor boy of Victorian fiction.

clue.text: Perhaps Mafiosi crimes — cell feature: to break them

indicators.note: the cell feature breaks into the crimes, splitting that word in two

parts.note: wrongdoings, here sins
cilia are the tiny hairlike projections on many cells

explanation.surface: Mafia crimes described as though a prison cell were part of the plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cell' suggests a prison, fitting the Mafia surface, but it is biology: CILIA. 'Perhaps' marks Mafiosi as an example of the islanders.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mafia originated on Sicily, so its members are an example of people from that island.

clue.text: Not anybody can be top dog

definitions.meaning: the leader, read as 'No. 1', number one

explanation.surface: A claim that nobody gets to be the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the answer as 'No. 1', number one, the one at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Nobody at all is the plain sense; the abbreviation for number one names whoever is the boss.

clue.text: Teacher finally failing head is in trouble

indicators.note: the last letter of the teacher's word is lost

parts.note: schoolchildren address a female teacher as Miss
a chief is the head of a group

explanation.surface: A teacher who fails a pupil and the headmaster ends up in hot water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is in' is just a link: the pieces sit side by side, not one inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Mischief means playful misbehaviour, the kind of trouble children get into.

clue.text: Trying to be mum? Oral inspection ordered

indicators.note: the letters of these two words are put in a new order

parts.note: fourteen letters rearranged into the Latin phrase

explanation.surface: A dental check-up being arranged by someone acting like a mother.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin phrase means 'in the place of a parent'; the question mark warns that being a mum is only an example of that role.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin legal phrase describes someone acting in the place of a parent, taking a mother's or father's role.

clue.text: Crown receiving attention humbly

parts.note: the crown of the head can be covered by a cap; crown and cap are both tops
a matter in hand is being dealt with

explanation.surface: A monarch's crown being looked after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crown' tempts the solver toward royalty, but it just means the top or cap. A petitioner once came holding their cap respectfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Approaching cap in hand means coming humbly, like a petitioner removing their hat to beg a favour.

clue.text: New learner's not to ask secret

indicators.note: the asking word is not in the learner's word, so it is removed

parts.note: a new learner is a beginner; the 's is 'is'
to beg is to ask earnestly

explanation.surface: A newcomer told they must not ask about a secret.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove BEG from BEGINNER to leave the five remaining letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner thoughts are private and hidden, so inner can mean secret.

clue.text: Joy is allowed to interrupt clairvoyant

indicators.note: the allowed word breaks into the clairvoyant word

parts.note: fey can mean having second sight
licit means lawful or allowed

explanation.surface: Happiness allowed to cut in on a fortune-teller.
explanation.definitionFit: Felicity is a formal word for great happiness, a synonym of joy.

clue.text: Joint operation making new start to encouraging cheers?

definitions.meaning: surgery replacing a worn hip joint

definitions.text: making new start to encouraging cheers?
definitions.meaning: the cheer 'hip hip hooray' starts with hip

explanation.surface: A surgical operation described as a fresh start for rousing applause.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: replacing the 'hip' at the start of 'hip hip hooray'.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgery replacing a damaged hip with an artificial one is a common joint operation.

clue.text: Made choice of college, say, as illustrated

indicators.note: the phrase is said aloud to sound like the answer

parts.note: picked Oriel, Oriel being an Oxford college

explanation.surface: A student choosing a college as shown in the pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: Oriel is a college of Oxford University; 'picked Oriel' said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pictorial book is one illustrated with pictures.

clue.text: Deliberately unpleasant organisation of 26

indicators.note: the letters of that answer are organised into a new order

parts.note: the answer to 26 across, a woodworker's tool

explanation.surface: Something nasty organised by an unnamed body.
explanation.walkthrough: Look up 26 across first; its five letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Penal conditions are punishing, designed to be harsh and unpleasant on purpose.

clue.text: Using sharp tool, scream, cutting head

indicators.note: the first letter is cut off

parts.note: to bawl is to scream or cry loudly

explanation.surface: Someone screaming as they use a sharp tool and cut their head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Using' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An awl is a small pointed tool for piercing holes in leather or wood.

clue.text: Almost wealthy with two coins, taking parochial view

parts.note: a euro is a coin
a cent is a coin

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is missing

parts.note: rich means wealthy

explanation.surface: Someone nearly rich with a couple of coins and a narrow outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the last letter of RICH. The two coins come in answer order, EURO then CENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A Eurocentric outlook sees the world only from a European angle, a narrow, parochial view.

clue.text: Struggling with budget purdah perhaps

indicators.note: the letters might form another word, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: the practice of screening women from view

explanation.surface: A household budget under strain while living in seclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: Purdah is the practice in some cultures of keeping women hidden; its letters are shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hard up means short of money, so struggling to make a budget stretch.

clue.text: The opposite of costing the earth?

definitions.text: The opposite of costing the earth?

parts.words: The opposite of costing the earth?
parts.note: costing the earth means very expensive; the opposite is costing next to nothing, with dirt playing on earth

explanation.surface: Something that does not cost the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: The play is on earth as soil: dirt is earth, so the cheap opposite of costing the earth costs only dirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extremely cheap costs as little as dirt, the opposite of costing a fortune.

clue.text: Short scenes as umpire resolves disputed call?

definitions.meaning: a few brief scenes make a short drama
in tennis a disputed serve can be ruled a let, and the umpire orders the point to be played again

explanation.surface: An umpire settling an argued line call.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis a let is a serve replayed; the umpire calls 'Let, play' to settle it, read here as the two words run together.
explanation.definitionFit: A playlet is a short play, a drama of only a few scenes.

clue.text: Love to spurn this key worker

definitions.text: Love to spurn this key worker

parts.words: Love to spurn this key worker
parts.note: the proverb says love laughs at the tradesman who makes locks, since no lock can keep lovers apart

explanation.surface: Love scorning a worker who deals with keys.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'Love laughs at locksmiths' says no lock keeps lovers apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who makes and repairs locks and keys is literally a worker with keys.

clue.text: Through windows, spot divine instrument

indicators.note: the spot goes through the windows, sitting inside them

parts.note: panes are glass sections of windows
a pip is a spot, as on dice or cards

explanation.surface: Glimpsing a holy instrument through a window.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay needs windows (PANES) to hold PIP; the OCR text dropped the S.
explanation.definitionFit: The god Pan played this set of reed pipes, making it the instrument of a divinity.

clue.text: Old empire is like modern country

parts.note: as means like
Syria is a present-day Middle Eastern country

explanation.surface: An ancient empire compared to a present-day nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Assyria was an ancient Mesopotamian empire centred on the Tigris.

clue.text: Concentrate, wanting to subdue

definitions.meaning: to boil down a sauce, making it more concentrated
to ... a city is to conquer or subdue it

explanation.surface: Someone trying to focus while wanting to subdue an enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting to' is a link joining the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooks boil a liquid down to thicken it; armies bring a fortress to submission. Both are senses of the word.

clue.text: Mark of infamy engulfs left dictator

indicators.note: the disgrace word swallows the letter

parts.note: a stain on one's character is a mark of disgrace

explanation.surface: A dictator's infamous record swallowing up the political left.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Stalin ruled the Soviet Union as a dictator.

clue.text: Good muscle, less fat — one's wiry, for a smoker

parts.note: pi is short for pious, meaning good
a pec is a chest muscle
leaner means less fat

explanation.surface: A fitness pitch about gaining muscle and losing fat for a wiry smoker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's wiry' describes the bendy wire tool used to clean a tobacco pipe; 'less fat' and 'wiry' fit the gym surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe smoker uses a fluffy wire stick to clear out the stem, so this item is wiry and for smokers.

clue.text: Count pence up — there's a piece of wisdom

indicators.note: in this down clue the pence letter goes up, above the count

parts.note: a count is a nobleman, equivalent to an earl

explanation.surface: A thoughtful remark about tallying pennies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' looks like a verb about money but is a noble rank. 'there's a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearl of wisdom is a wise saying, so the gem stands for a nugget of insight.

clue.text: Comfortably large jumper, wow!

parts.note: a roo, a kangaroo, is a jumper
'my!' is an exclamation of surprise, like 'wow!'

explanation.surface: A pleasingly loose sweater that draws admiration.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a jumper is a sweater, which the surface uses; here it is the leaping kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: Roomy means spacious, with plenty of space, comfortably large.

clue.text: Order dog to behave, as magistrates do

definitions.meaning: the command given to a dog to stay seated
a court is said to be in session when magistrates hear cases

explanation.surface: Telling a dog to behave in the way a bench of magistrates does.
explanation.walkthrough: Magistrates are lay judges in English local courts; when a court is in session it is said to be sitting.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the word of command to a dog, and the verb for judges holding a court session.

clue.text: Course on power tool

indicators.note: in an across clue the course word comes on, after, the power letter

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics
a lane is a course, as in a running track

explanation.surface: A course on how to use a power tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'power tool' reads as one phrase, but 'power' is wordplay and 'tool' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plane is a carpenter's tool for smoothing wood.

clue.text: Mirror reflection?

parts.note: the Daily Mirror is a British newspaper, and its leader article reflects its opinion

explanation.surface: An image seen in a looking-glass.
explanation.walkthrough: The Daily Mirror is a British tabloid; its considered view, its reflection, appears in a leading article.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's leading article gives its reflections on the news.

clue.text: Ruth turned in on herself, an ignoble feeling

indicators.note: the pity is directed onto oneself, placed after the self word

parts.note: self, the person concerned
ruth is an old word for pity

explanation.surface: A woman named Ruth turned inward and wallowing in an unworthy emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruth' looks like a woman's name but is the old word for compassion, as in 'ruthless'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wallowing in sorrow for one's own troubles is usually seen as an unworthy, ignoble emotion.

clue.text: Mark, man from Israeli port speaking?

indicators.note: the word is said aloud to give the answer

parts.note: a native of Haifa, a port in Israel, could be called a Haifan

explanation.surface: A man named Mark from Israel's port, speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name; it is the definition, a punctuation mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A short dash joining words is a punctuation mark.
